newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angolan minister accuses U.N. staff of child sex.
newsitem.headline: Angolan minister accuses U.N. staff of child sex.

text.p: Angola's Justice Minister Paulo Tjipilica on Friday accused United Nations personnel and foreign aid workers in Angola of sexually exploiting children.

"Aside from Angolan citizens there are foreigners involved (in child sexual exploitation), some who work for UNAVEM (U.N. Angola Verification Mission) and others who work with aid groups," Tjipilica told a conference on child abuse.
U.N. spokesman David Wimhurst told Reuters a committee had been set up to investigate allegations of child sexual abuse by U.N. personnel working in Angola.
"We are aware that allegations have been made against U.N, personnel here," Wimhurst said.

"We have recently formed a committee to investigate this matter but the committee has not returned with a full report. We certainly would deplore such behaviour if this turned out to be true, but we cannot really comment until the committee has finished its work," he added.
The head of an aid agency working with children in Angola said her organisation had conducted a study last year and found an increase in the number of child prostitutes in the capital Luanda.
"We interviewed a number of people who made allegations of U.N. personnel being involved in this. But, we found no direct evidence to support the allegations," said said.

About 7,000 U.N. peackeepers from countries including Zimbabwe, Zambia, Brazil, Uruguay, the Netherlands, Zaire, India and France have been in Angola since 1995 to help implement a 1994 peace agreement between the government and former rebel UNITA movement after almost two decades of civil war.
The mission, one of the biggest deployed by the U.N., is set to begin a gradual withdrawal from the end of February.
